before.clause: Let $Y$ be a closed connected oriented rational homology three-sphere, let $\mathfrak t$ be a Spin$^c$ structure, and suppose the Heegaard Floer groups, absolute rational grading, and natural map $\iota_*:HF^\infty(Y,\mathfrak t)\to HF^+(Y,\mathfrak t)$ are defined and independent of the construction choices. View $HF^+$ as an $\mathbb F_2[U]$-module. An element is $U$-torsion if some positive power of $U$ annihilates it. The correction term $d(Y,\mathfrak t)$ is the minimum absolute grading of a $U$-nontorsion element in $\operatorname{im}\iota_*$. The standard normalization is $d(S^3,\mathfrak t_0)=0$ for the unique Spin$^c$ structure $\mathfrak t_0$ on $S^3$. Existence of the minimum and independence of choices are separate proof obligations.

after.clause: Let $Y$ be a closed connected oriented rational homology three-sphere, let $\mathfrak t$ be a Spin$^c$ structure, and suppose the Heegaard Floer groups, absolute rational grading, and natural map $\iota_*:HF^\infty(Y,\mathfrak t)\to HF^+(Y,\mathfrak t)$ are defined and independent of the construction choices. View $HF^+$ as an $\mathbb F_2[U]$-module. An element is $U$-torsion if some positive power of $U$ annihilates it. The correction term $d(Y,\mathfrak t)$ is the minimum absolute grading of a nonzero homogeneous element in $\operatorname{im}\iota_*$. In the standard plus tower every element is $U$-torsion, although every element is divisible by every positive power of $U$; these two properties are compatible. The definition uses the nonzero homogeneous image elements, rather than imposing $U$-nontorsion. The standard normalization is $d(S^3,\mathfrak t_0)=0$ for the unique Spin$^c$ structure $\mathfrak t_0$ on $S^3$. Existence of the minimum and independence of choices are separate proof obligations.

before.clause: For every closed connected oriented rational homology three-sphere $Y$ and Spin$^c$ structure $\mathfrak t$, the standard Heegaard Floer groups $HF^\infty(Y,\mathfrak t)$ and $HF^+(Y,\mathfrak t)$ constructed from admissible pointed Heegaard diagrams are independent, up to grading-preserving isomorphism, of the diagram and regular auxiliary data. The image of $HF^\infty\to HF^+$ has a non-torsion $U$-tower bounded below in the absolute rational grading, so its minimum grading $d(Y,\mathfrak t)$ exists and is independent of choices. The normalization is $d(S^3,\mathfrak t_0)=0$.

after.clause: For every closed connected oriented rational homology three-sphere $Y$ and Spin$^c$ structure $\mathfrak t$, the standard Heegaard Floer groups $HF^\infty(Y,\mathfrak t)$ and $HF^+(Y,\mathfrak t)$ constructed from admissible pointed Heegaard diagrams are independent, up to grading-preserving isomorphism, of the diagram and regular auxiliary data. The image of $HF^\infty\to HF^+$ is a graded plus tower, isomorphic as an $\mathbb F_2[U]$-module to $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]/U\mathbb F_2[U]$ with an absolute rational grading shift and with $U$ of degree $-2$. Its nonzero homogeneous elements have a least grading; this least grading $d(Y,\mathfrak t)$ exists and is independent of choices. Every tower element is $U$-torsion and is divisible by every power of $U$. The normalization is $d(S^3,\mathfrak t_0)=0$.

concrete_counterexample.calculation: For v=sum(j=0..J)c_j U^-j, U^(J+1)v=0. In particular U*1=0. Thus no U-nontorsion image element exists even for the standard S3 tower; its nonzero homogeneous occupied degrees are 0,2,4,... with minimum0.
concrete_counterexample.corrected_clause: Minimum grading of a nonzero homogeneous image element; local U-torsion is compatible with divisibility by every power.

scope_preserved: Every rational homology sphere, every SpinC structure, full absolutegrading and invariance claims retained.
